The XGBoost NFL model operates as a decision-tree ensemble that aggregates multiple weak learners to predict outcomes such as win probability and playoff likelihood. It leverages NFLverse-style features including quarterback efficiency, explosive play rate, turnover margin, pass rush metrics, point differentials, and player availability. These inputs are adjusted for roster changes through scalar modifiers. Monte Carlo simulations run 10,000 iterations to estimate season outcomes. The highlight reel detector uses audiovisual signals—specifically crowd noise spikes and commentary cues—to identify touchdown and interception events automatically. This system relies on signal processing techniques to correlate acoustic and visual anomalies with game events. The defensive coverage analyzer classifies pre- and post-snap alignments into man, zone, or blitz coverages, enabling tracking of team tendencies. Each primitive contributes to a larger framework where probabilistic inference and pattern recognition inform strategic decisions in real time. Failure modes include overfitting due to limited feature diversity, misclassification of dynamic plays, and breakdown in audio-visual correlation under noisy conditions.
